In re : Ia No. Can 2 of 2023 The application being Ia No. Can 2 of 2023 has been filed by one Dr.
Sunanda Goenka (in short, Sunanda) praying for leave to prefer appeal against the order dated 12th
October, 2023 passed by the learned Single Judge in a writ petition being Wpa 24065 of 2023.

Mr. Sanyal, learned advocate appearing for the applicant/appellant submits that by the order dated 12 th October, 2023 the learned Single Judge arrived at a finding that the Anti-Fraud Section had failed to investigate the matter properly and accordingly directed the Criminal Investigation Department (in short, CID) of the State to start investigation pertaining to Charumarket Police S t a t i o n C a s e N o . 1 9 1 o f 2 0 1 8 d a t e d 1 5 t h N o v e m b e r , 2 0 1 8 u n d e r S e c t i o n s 406/420/467/468/471/120B of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as Case No.191 of 2018).

The impugned order puts forth a threat perception that the applicant would be arrested in connection with such investigation and as a consequence, her constitutional right would be adversely affected.

Mr. De Dhar, learned advocate appearing for the writ petitioner/respondent no.1 herein denies the contention of the applicant and submits that the accused persons do not have a say in the matter of appointment of an investigation agency and the applicant's presence is not necessary for adjudication of the lis.

In support of such submission reliance has been placed upon the judgment delivered in the case of Narmada Bai Vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2011) 5 SCC 79 and the Dr. Sunanda Goenka vs Neil Basu & Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134125529/

sentences.text: Mr. Nandy, learned advocate enters appearance on behalf of the State respondents and submits that the fact that the applicant was not impleaded as a party respondent in the writ petition cannot be a ground to label the impugned order as unsustainable inasmuch as an accused does not have any right to be heard at the stage of investigation.

In support of the argument advanced reliance has been placed upon the judgment delivered in the case of Sri Bhagwan Samardha Sreepada Vallabha Venkata Vishwanandha Maharaj Vs. State of A.P. & ors., reported in (1999) 5 SCC 740.

sentences.text: It is well known that a decision is an authority for what it decides and not what can logically be deduced therefrom.
Even a slight distinction in fact or an additional fact may make a lot of difference in decision making process.
The judgment is a precedent for the issue of law that is raised and decided and not observations made in the facts of any particular case.
Plentitude of pronouncements leaves cleavage in the opinions formed in the respective cases.
There is no dispute as regards the proposition of law as laid down in the judgments upon which reliance has been placed by Mr. Sanyal, however, the same are distinguishable on facts.

The judgment in the case of E.
Sivakumar (supra) was delivered in a case involving manufacture and sale of gutkha and pan masala having national ramifications.
The judgment in the case of Narmada Bai (supra) was delivered in a case involving police atrocities and death.
The basic entitlement of every citizen, who is faced with allegations of criminal wrong doing is that the investigative process should be fair.
This is an integral component of the guarantee against arbitrariness under Article 14 and of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

The primary allegation in the complaint lodged by the writ petitioner was that the applicant and others had no qualification for the teaching posts which they were holding at Jogesh Chandra Chaudhuri Law College (hereinafter referred to as the said College).
In course of investigation, the accused persons were interrogated and thereafter a final report was filed on 23 rd April, 2022.
The writ petition was filed about 1 years thereafter on 4th October, 2023.
The matter was heard and the order was passed by the learned Single Judge on 12th October, 2023 engaging a new investigating agency.

The learned Single Judge in the order impugned had inter alia observed as follows:
"one order passed in CRR 3568 of 2019 in the matter of Smt. Sunanda Goenka has been produced before me as well as the case diary.
In respect of this CRR 3568 of 2019 there was an order of this court for not taking any coercive step till 05.02.2022 that has expired more than three years ago.
Therefore, today there is no impediment for the Investigating Agency if the C.I.D. takes steps forthwith in all respects against the said Smt. Sunanda Goenka".
From a perusal of the said order, the threat perception of the applicant cannot totally be ruled out.

In view thereof and for determination of the issue as to whether the parameters towards exercise of extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India have been established, the presence of the applicant would be necessary.
The FIR was registered way back in the year 2018.
In course of investigation, the investigating agency did not exercise its right to arrest, which indicates that the petitioner joined the investigation.

At this belated stage and on the basis of the impugned Dr. Sunanda Goenka vs Neil Basu & Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134125529/
2 order passed in the writ petition, CID has been left with no option but to curtail the liberty of the applicant in breach of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and as such we consider it expedient to grant leave to the applicant to prefer the present appeal.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the applicant's prayer for leave to appeal is allowed and the application being IA No.
CAN 2 of 2023 is disposed of.
In connection with the appeal, the applicant/appellant, namely, Smt. Sunanda Goenka had also filed an application for stay being CAN No.1 of 2023.

Drawing our attention to the averments made in the writ petition annexed to the stay application,
Mr. Sanyal argues that the writ petitioner has inter alia stated that he took admission in the said College in LLB five year Bachelor Course in the year 2013 and graduated from the said College in 2018.
In the midst thereof, he was elected as the General Secretary of the said College and accordingly he was inducted in the Governing Body as an ex-officio member.

However, the writ petition has been affirmed by him on 4th October, 2023, about five years after he left the College,
seeking direction for de novo investigation pertaining to a case in which, upon completion of investigation, the Anti-Fraud Section of Detective Department filed the final report.
The said sequence of facts does not reveal infringement of any legal right of the writ petitioner and as such the writ petition itself was not maintainable.
He argues that the complaint was initially lodged by the writ petitioner in the year 2018 and upon completion of the investigation FRT was submitted on 23 rd April, 2022.
The writ petitioner had full knowledge of such fact but he did not file any Naraji/Protest petition.

The matter appeared before the jurisdictional Magistrate on 10 th November, 2022, 12th January, 2023 and 9th August, 2023 but on none of the said occasions, the writ petitioner appeared before the learned Magistrate.

The next date has been fixed on 28 th November, 2023 and as such the issue as to whether the said FRT would be accepted or as to whether further investigation would be directed, is still pending before the learned Magistrate.

The issue agitated is as to whether without taking appropriate steps as provided under the ordinary criminal jurisdiction, the writ petitioner could have approached this Court seeking de novo investigation that too about 1 years after final report was submitted before the learned Magistrate.

In support of the arguments reliance has been placed upon the judgments delivered in the cases of Devendra Nath Singh Vs. State of Bihar & ors. reported in (2023) 1 SCC 48;
Chandra Babu alias Moses Vs. State through Inspector of Police & ors., reported in (2015) 8 SCC 774 and Pooja Pal Vs. Union of India & ors., reported in (2016) 3 SCC 135.

The allegations are grave and the matter needs to be thoroughly investigated.
In the support of the arguments reliance has been placed upon an unreported judgment delivered in the case of State of West Bengal - vs- Soumen Nandy & Ors.

3 Mr. De Dhar, learned advocate appearing for the writ petitioner/respondent no.1 submits that the facts reveal a very sorry state of affairs.
A complaint was lodged by him in the year 2018 which was registered as the Case no.191 of 2018.
In spite of repeated representations, no steps were taken by the police authorities and in a most illegal and malafide manner a final report was filed about four years after the complaint was lodged.
To unearth the truth, the only option the petitioner had was to approach this Court for invocation of jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

He argues that undeserved persons had been accorded unfair advantage over the deserved and considering the extraordinary dimension of the offence, the Court had directed CID to fresh investigation and there is no infirmity in the exercise of such discretion.
Heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and considered the materials on record.

Prima facie, the order appears to have been passed taking into consideration the fact that though the offence alleged was cognizable and punishable for more than seven years, a Section 41A notice was issued and the Anti-Fraud Section avoided to ascertain the Rules and Regulations on the basis of which Commission recommended the appellant.
It is well-settled that inherent powers cannot be exercised by the constitutional Court in a routine manner.
Issuance of any direction for de novo investigation must be exercised with great caution.
The contextual facts and the attendant circumstances have to be singularly evaluated and analysed to decide the needfulness of de novo investigation.
Indisputably, the fact that upon completion of investigation, final report had been submitted in the Case No.191 of 2018 was within the knowledge of the writ petitioner.
It was also within his knowledge that the said final report has not yet been accepted by the learned Magistrate.
He did not file any Naraji/Protest petition before the learned Magistrate.
The final report was filed on 23rd April, 2022.
The writ petition was, however, filed on 4th October, 2023.
Initially investigation was conducted by the respondent no.6.
Subsequent thereto, investigation was handed over to Anti-Fraud Section.

The report was filed by the Anti-Fraud Section on 23 rd April, 2022 and by the order impugned, direction was given to hand over the investigation to CID and the matter was made returnable five days thereafter on 17 th October, 2023 at 1.00 pm with a direction upon the State to file a preliminary report.
Such sequence of facts prima facie reflects an unusual haste to proceed with the matter.
The learned Magistrate has the power to direct further investigation.
Neither the scheme of the Code nor any specific provision therein bars exercise of such jurisdiction by the learned Magistrate.
The issue as regards acceptance of final report

is pending before the learned Magistrate and without entering appearance before the learned Magistrate on three consecutive dates, i.e. on 10th November, 2022, 12th January, 2023 and 9th August, 2023, the writ petitioner approached this Court on 4th October, 2023.

In the said conspectus, whether he could have filed the writ petition praying for de novo investigation ought to have been examined and decided by the learned Single Judge prior to issuance of the order impugned.

The above issue in our opinion requires adjudication Dr. Sunanda Goenka vs Neil Basu & Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134125529/
4 upon exchange of affidavits.
